# SPE round 3 plan

## Where round 2 left us

Round 2 predictions hit 1 of 5. The naive "same as last round" guess was closer on the other 4. So in round 3 every number stays at its round 2 value unless a stated change moves it. The stop rule needs 3 matching rounds in a row, and the count is 0, so the loop continues.

## Specify

### Decisions on the round 3 proposals

| ID | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Adopt | F4 shows C never called the outage status check while it sat inside the merged tool. Splitting it out is C's one change this round. |
| P2 | Adopt, as a separate "hard" set | A and B are at 0.86, near the ceiling. The r02 tickets stay unchanged as the "core" set, so the same-as-last-round numbers still apply to them. |
| P3 | Adopt | D was last on category accuracy (0.74) and its cost rose from $0.003 to $0.004. Fixing F6 would be a new change to a config we are not choosing. F6 closes as "config dropped". |
| P4 | Adopt | B's r02 miss was inside noise at n=3. Five trials per cell narrows the bands. |

### Round 3 requirements (added to `spe/spec/spec.md`)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R3.1 | Config C exposes the outage status check as its own tool. The rest of C's merge stays as it was. | r02 F4, P1 | C's tool list contains the status tool. Transcripts show a status call on outage tickets. |
| R3.2 | Add 10 hard tickets that mix billing and outage. Score them as a separate "hard" set. | P2 | `spe/evals/tickets/hard-r03.yaml` has 10 tickets with labels. Results are reported for core and hard separately. |
| R3.3 | Run configs A, B, C only. | P3, r02 F6 | The Workflow `configs` argument is `["A","B","C"]`. |
| R3.4 | Run 5 trials per cell. | P4 | Each cell has 5 graded trials or a logged skip. |
| R3.5 | The grader reads priority from `label.priority` and never from the draft reply. | r02 F5 | A selftest case has a draft reply that says P1 and a label that says P3. It must grade as P3. |
| R3.6 | The core ticket set is the r02 set with no changes. | Predict rule (same as last round) | The core ticket file hash matches r02. |
| R3.7 | Every trial logs tokens and cost. | Decision: D was the only cost baseline | Each trial record has `usage.cost_usd`. |

Rows from rounds 1 and 2 carry forward unchanged.

### Defaults logged in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`

- I will draft the 10 hard tickets and their labels. The rule is that the category is the ask the customer wants solved first. Priority follows the existing rule, so an active outage sets P1 or P2. The user can review `hard-r03.yaml` before launch. A bad label would be a broken grader.
- D is dropped rather than fixed. The user can reverse this at approval.
- Priority accuracy is predicted for C only, as it was in round 2.

## Predict

A hit means the measured value falls inside the band. Each config changes one thing at most. A and B do not change. C splits out the status tool. The hard set and n=5 apply to every config the same way, and the hard set is scored separately.

| Metric | Set | Config | Same as last round | Predicted | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category accuracy | core | A | 0.86 | 0.86 ± 0.04 | `grade.py`: `label.category` exact match to key | A does not change. |
| category accuracy | core | B | 0.86 | 0.86 ± 0.04 | same | B does not change. The r02 guess of 0.88 assumed a gain that did not appear. |
| category accuracy | core | C | 0.80 | 0.82 ± 0.04 | same | The split undoes part of the r02 merge. I move it only 0.02 because the F4 evidence is about priority and not category. |
| priority accuracy | core | C | 0.71 | 0.77 ± 0.05 | `grade.py`: `label.priority` exact match | F4 says outage tickets got P3 because the lookup was hidden. Restoring the lookup should bring C back near its r01 value of 0.78, but not above it. |
| outage lookup rate (outage tickets) | core | C | 0.00 | 0.90 ± 0.10 | Code check: the transcript has a status tool call | C will see the separate tool in its tool list, as it did in r01. |
| category accuracy | hard | A | none (new set) | 0.70 ± 0.10 | `label.category` exact match to the hard key | The tickets are built to sit below the 0.86 ceiling. The band is wide because there is no baseline. |
| category accuracy | hard | B | none | 0.70 ± 0.10 | same | Same reason as A. |
| category accuracy | hard | C | none | 0.70 ± 0.10 | same | Same reason as A. |
| priority accuracy | hard | C | none | 0.65 ± 0.10 | `label.priority` exact match | Mixed tickets make priority harder to call, even with the lookup. |
| cost per ticket | all | A, B, C | none | measured only | `usage.cost_usd` mean | There is no baseline because D was the only config with a cost number. Round 4 will predict cost. |

## Evaluate

### Gates before launch (halt on any failure)

1. Grader selftest. The oracle passes. Empty and wrong answers fail. The F5 case from R3.5 grades P3. A hard-set oracle passes.
2. Control regrade. The current `grade.py` regrades all r02 transcripts. It must reproduce the regraded r02 numbers exactly: category A 0.86, B 0.86, C 0.80, D 0.74, and C priority 0.71.
3. Dry run on 3 cells: C on T17 (where F4 was seen), A on one hard ticket, and B on one core ticket. Check the schema, the tool-call log, and the cost log. Project the full cost from the measured per-trial cost.

### Workflow run

- `const ROUND = 3` is the only place the round number appears.
- Arguments: `configs: ["A","B","C"]`, `sets: ["core","hard"]`, `trialsPerCell: 5`, `extraTrialsPerSplitCell: 3`, `maxExtraTrials: 60`, `budgetCapUsd: 20`. Models and prompts stay as in r02 except for C's tool list.
- Trial schema: `{ticket_id, label: {category, priority}, draft_reply, tool_calls[], usage: {tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd}}`.
- Code checks only. No judge is needed, because every metric is checkable by code.
- Peek scan: void any trial whose transcript reads `grade.py`, the answer keys, `hard-r03.yaml` labels, or `spe/predictions/`. Log the voids.
- Budget: skip any trial that would cross the cap, and log the skip.
- Split cells, where trials disagree, get up to 3 extra trials within the 60-trial cap.
- End with a failure analysis and a completeness critic.

### Cost estimate (not measured)

The pasted context does not give the core ticket count. I assume 20 for this estimate and will use the real count from the ticket file. That gives 3 configs × 30 tickets × 5 trials = 450 trials, plus up to 60 extra. I have no measured per-trial cost for A, B, or C, so I use $0.02 as a placeholder. The total is about $10.20 against a $20 cap. If the dry run projects more than $20, I halt and report before the full launch.

### Halt and report if

The budget cap is hit. An answer key leaks into a trial. The selftest or the control regrade fails. A hard-ticket label needs the user's call.

Do not edit after the run.` It includes the round, the date, the author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", the configs, every number with its band and Why, and `same_as_last_round`. Leave `r03-draft.yaml` as it is. Commit `SPE r03 predict: C splits status tool, hard set, n=5`.
3. Write `hard-r03.yaml`, the new selftest cases, and `spe/evals/harness/r03-workflow.js`. Commit `SPE r03 evaluate (harness)`.
4. Run the 3 gates, then launch the Workflow.
5. When the completion notice arrives, commit `SPE r03 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
6. Learn. Add the round 3 section to `prediction-log.md` with "Which Why broke", and say plainly whether the naive guess won again. Update `failures.md`, including F6 marked as config dropped. Add "Proposed for round 4" to the spec, write `r04-draft.yaml`, and update `README.md`. Commit `SPE r03 learn: ...` and tag `spe-r03`.

All commits stay local. Nothing is pushed.
